programme: NCOA4-driven ferritinophagy: NCOA4 delivers ferritin to autophagic degradation to release chelatable iron, fueling iron-dependent lipid peroxidation (ferroptosis); its inferred prostate targets AR, KLK3 and TFF1 reflect its separate, established role as the androgen-receptor coactivator ARA70, driving AR-dependent transcription in the same cells.
role_in_a: In prostate cancer NCOA4 has a dual identity: as ARA70 it coactivates AR to drive AR-target transcription (consistent with its network edges to AR, KLK3/PSA and TFF1), and separately its ferritinophagy activity can be induced to disrupt androgen biosynthesis and trigger ferroptotic death in AR-dependent tumor cells, with germline NCOA4 variants also reported to associate with PCa risk.
role_in_b: In ischemic stroke, NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy releases iron from ferritin during ischemia-reperfusion, driving lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic loss of oxygen/glucose-deprived cells; the retrieved work operates on the vascular/blood side of injury (endothelial progenitor cell exosomes, KLF6/NSUN2 regulation of NCOA4, electroacupuncture) rather than on brain parenchyma directly.
shared_axis: Both diseases converge on the same iron-mobilizing engine — NCOA4-dependent ferritinophagy — deployed to opposite ends: as a therapeutic vulnerability to kill AR-dependent tumor cells in prostate cancer, and as a pathological driver of ischemia-reperfusion cell death in stroke. The AR-coactivator function is prostate-specific and does not extend to stroke, so the cross-disease link runs through the ferroptosis arm only.
reasoning: No retrieved paper states a direct prostate cancer–stroke connection, so this is not established; but each disease independently has multiple on-topic, non-review papers placing NCOA4 in ferroptosis biology specific to that disease, and the module (ferritinophagy) is nameable from NCOA4 alone, which meets the bar for supported/strong rather than a reasoning-only moderate call.
support: PMID 40446866 (PCa: NCOA4-driven ferroptosis disrupts androgen biosynthesis, suppresses tumor growth); PMID 37667572 (PCa: NCOA4 in the AR interactome, consistent with its ARA70 coactivator role); PMID 22887727 (PCa: NCOA4 genetic variants associated with prostate cancer risk); PMID 42603839 (Stroke: EPC-derived exosomes reduce ferroptosis and promote neovascularization post-stroke); PMID 41478321 (Stroke: KLF6-activated NSUN2 m5C-modifies NCOA4 to enhance ferroptosis in OGD/R injury); PMID 40189641 (Stroke: electroacupuncture modulates ferroptosis mechanisms in ischemic stroke).
how_to_falsify: Deplete NCOA4 in parallel in an AR-positive prostate cancer line and an OGD/R (or MCAO-derived endothelial/neuronal) ischemia-reperfusion model; measure labile iron pool and lipid ROS/MDA with and without ferrostatin-1 rescue. If NCOA4 loss fails to blunt ferroptotic markers in both systems, the shared ferritinophagy axis is wrong. Separately, if NCOA4 knockdown does not reduce AR-target expression (KLK3, TFF1) in the prostate model, the coactivator half of the account is also wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|prostate, so the 'stroke' evidence here is largely vascular/circulating (endothelial progenitor cells, peripheral OGD/R models) rather than direct CNS neuronal data — treat the stroke role as reperfusion-injury biology, not proven brain-parenchymal mechanism. Support is 29 of 51 patient-group comparisons across 4 cohort pairs (~57%), a real majority but not overwhelming. The single-view exclusions (KAT6A, STAT6, JUNB, etc.) were correctly left out since none recur beyond one subgroup. The tissue-generic exclusions (ERG, STAT3, NFATC2, JUNB, SPIB and others) remove the usual PCa/blood master regulators, which is why the account does not reach for ERG or STAT3 despite their prominence in these tissues. Other concordant factors with real but separate evidence — IRF9 (interferon-stimulated gene response) and SIM2 (hypoxia/PAS network in PCa, but its stroke hits are off-topic catheter-device results) — were deliberately excluded from this account because they represent distinct pathways from NCOA4-ferroptosis, not because they lack support; folding them in would overstate a single coherent module.
